By Drew Dorian

Overview

The three-row Hyundai Palisade is built on a platform shared with the superb Kia Telluride. Thanks to that connection, the first-generation Palisade has also been a great choice in the mid-size crossover segment since its debut as a 2020 model, but this new second-generation version is coming in hot with a fresh design. Boxier lines and cool details like the wide, silver D-pillar give the Palisade a more modern presence.

The 2026 Palisade remains a three-row SUV with a maximum seating capacity of eight. A V-6 engine is standard and makes 287 horsepower. The cabin is premium and thoughtfully equipped with convenience features, and the top-spec Calligraphy trim offers Genesis-like luxury.

Expert Tip: Hyundai also offers the Palisade with a 329-hp hybrid powertrain, but we review that model separately.

What's New for 2026?

The Palisade enters its second generation for the 2026 model year, and it grows slightly over the previous model with a longer wheelbase and slightly bigger exterior dimensions. Blockier styling with bold lighting elements aligns the new Palisade's appearance with Hyundai’s new electric Ioniq 9 SUV, and the revamped interior wears a contemporary appearance and posh materials.

A rugged-looking XRT Pro model rides on a raised suspension and offers terrain-specific driving modes while luxury-oriented Calligraph trim continues to offer a class-above interior experience.

Pricing and Which One to Buy

The SEL Premium trim offers the best balance between affordability and features. The upgrade from the SEL trim adds nice-to-have features such as ventilated front seats, heated rear seats, a 360-degree camera system, and a heated steering wheel.

Engine, Transmission, and Performance

  • Engine: 287-hp 3.5-liter V-6
  • Transmission: 8-speed automatic
  • Drivetrains: front-wheel-drive, all-wheel-drive

A 287-hp, 3.5-liter V-6 engine is standard on the Palisade. An eight-speed automatic transmission comes on every model, but you can choose from either front- or all-wheel drive. A 329-hp hybrid setup is also available, but we review the Palisade Hybrid separately.

The more rugged XRT Pro model rides on a lifted suspension with an extra inch of ground clearance versus other Palisades. It also comes with driver-selectable terrain modes for optimizing traction in mud, sand, and snow.

While the V-6 doesn't deliver particularly exciting acceleration, it is powerful enough for casual driving. Handling is bland, but the ride is comfortable and well-suited for family duty.

0–60-MPH Times

  • C/D 60-mph Test: 8.0–8.1 seconds

In Comparison: In our testing, the Palisade Calligraphy got to 60 mph in 8.0 seconds and the XRT did it in 8.1 seconds. That's on the slow end of the class and significantly slower than the old model, largely due to the new model's extra weight.

    Towing and Payload Capacity

    The 2026 Palisade is rated to tow as much as 5000 pounds, and all-wheel drive versions come with a dedicated tow mode that programs the automatic transmission to hold lower gears longer. XRT Pro, Limited, and Calligraphy trims come standard with an integrated hitch that’s hidden behind a panel on the Palisade’s rear bumper.

    Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG

    • EPA City Ratings: 18-19 mpg
    • EPA Highway Ratings: 24-25 mpg
    • C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel Economy Test: 25 mpg

    The front-wheel drive Palisade model is rated by the EPA for 19 mpg city, 25 mpg highway, and 21 mpg combined. Add all-wheel drive, and those numbers drop by an even 1 mpg across the board.

    On our 75-mph highway fuel economy route, the all-wheel-drive Palisade Calligraphy achieved 25 mpg. For more information about the Palisade's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

    Interior, Comfort, and Cargo

    First Row: The three-row Palisade offers seating for the whole family, but the first row is particularly spacious, and the rounded edges of the dashboard are inspired by mid-century-modern furniture. Overall, the interior has a premium look and feel, especially in the top Calligraphy trim, which offers class-above finishes and standard equipment. Lesser trims still offer plenty of comfort and convenience gear. The cabin is dotted with cupholders and USB-C charging ports, and features such as a wireless smartphone charging pad, a UV-C sanitizing tray, and a digital rear-view mirror are available.

    Second Row: Thanks to a standard three-person second-row bench seat, the Palisade can seat eight, but a pair of optional second-row captain’s chairs that can recline and deploy footrests for maximum lounge-ability drop the passenger count to seven.

    Third Row: The Palisade's rearmost bench seat is plenty spacious for children and will hold an adult on occasion. On upper trims, the third row is power-adjustable with redundant controls in the cargo area, which is convenient for times when you need to drop the seats to accommodate cargo.

    Cargo Capacity: Behind the third row of seats, the Palisade offers only 19.1 cubic feet of space. With the rearmost seats stowed, cargo capacity balloons to a generous 46.3 cubic feet, which should be plenty for road trips and large grocery hauls. When we get a chance, we'll stuff the 2026 Palisade with carry-on suitcases and update this story with results.

    Infotainment and Connectivity

    A large, curved display houses two 12.3-inch screens and provides the driver access to gauges and infotainment. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are both standard, as is an on-board Wi-Fi hotspot, in-dash navigation, Amazon Alexa, and an in-car payment technology called Hyundai Pay. A 14-speaker Bose stereo system is optional.

    Safety and Driver-Assistance Features

    All Palisades come equipped with a host of driver-assistance features, including expected basics such as automated emergency braking, an adaptive cruise control system, and lane-keeping assist. A more advanced adaptive cruise control system with a lane-centering feature is optional.

    • Standard Safety Features: automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control
    • Optional Safety Features: adaptive cruise control with lane-centering, parking sensors

    For more information about the Palisade's crash test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

    Warranty and Maintenance Coverage

    Hyundai's warranty is one of the best in the business, highlighted by the 10-year, 100,000-mile powertrain coverage for the first owner of the vehicle. Starting with 2026 models, there is no complimentary scheduled maintenance plan.

    • Limited Warranty: five years or 60,000 miles
    • Powertrain Warranty: 10 years or 100,000 miles
    • Complimentary Maintenance: None
